investment_summary:
Autodesk's fiscal 2026 showed accelerating top-line momentum: revenue rose 18% to $7.21 billion, 97% of it recurring, and free cash flow reached $2.38 billion [1]. Profit lagged. Operating margin held at 22%, and net income rose only 1% as restructuring costs reached $216 million and tax expense climbed [1].

Consensus expects revenue growth of 16.1% in FY2027 and 10.7% in FY2028, with normalized EPS of $12.80 for FY2027 [3]. At $246.78, the reverse DCF implies 11.3% annual revenue growth for ten years at an 11.1% WACC [2][3]. That is close to the historical 12.9% three-year revenue CAGR [2], so the valuation requires Autodesk to sustain roughly its past growth for a decade. The consensus path yields an implied return of 9.5%, below the WACC, which leaves little margin for error [3]. Main risks are the shift to annual billing, 64% international exposure and AI-driven competition [1]. Consensus and valuation figures are dated after the 10-K.
key_takeaways: Growth should stay strong as AECO scales: revenue rose 18% and AECO grew 22% to $3.58 billion [1].
Earnings quality needs to improve: GAAP operating margin stayed at 22% while restructuring and commissions absorbed the gains [1].
Valuation looks full: the consensus path implies a 9.5% return, below the 11.1% WACC, so returns depend on growth beating forecasts [3].
Cash generation supports buybacks: free cash flow of $2.38 billion covered $1.40 billion of repurchases, though working capital absorbed $501 million [1].
business_overview:
Autodesk, Inc. is a global 3D design, engineering and entertainment technology company. It sells software to architecture, engineering and construction (AECO), manufacturing, and media and entertainment customers. In fiscal 2026, which ended January 31, 2026, net revenue rose 18% to $7.21 billion from $6.13 billion, and 97% of it was recurring [1]. Subscription revenue reached $6.74 billion, and current remaining performance obligations grew 23% to $5.48 billion, which is a useful guide to contracted revenue over the next twelve months [1]. Net revenue retention stayed above the 100% to 110% range on a constant currency basis at both year ends [1]. Core products include Revit, AutoCAD and AutoCAD LT, AutoCAD Civil 3D, Autodesk Build, Fusion, Inventor, Maya and 3ds Max [1].

Growth is concentrated in AECO. That family rose 22% to $3.58 billion and added $646 million, the largest dollar gain of any family, on AEC Collections, enterprise business agreements (EBA) and Autodesk Construction Cloud, now called Forma for Construction [1]. AutoCAD and AutoCAD LT grew 14% to $1.79 billion, Manufacturing grew 16% to $1.38 billion, and Media and Entertainment grew 5% to $332 million [1]. The Media and Entertainment figure is flattered by lower contra revenue under the new transaction model, so underlying demand there is weaker than the headline suggests [1]. Other revenue, mainly consulting and training, rose 6% to $125 million [1].

The most important strategic change is the new transaction model. Solution Providers now quote prices while Autodesk contracts directly with the customer. That moved the direct channel to 63% of revenue from 42%, and cut TD Synnex's share to 14% from 33% [1]. Management is also reallocating resources toward cloud, platform and AI. Restructuring and exit costs rose to $216 million from $15 million, the company spent $1.40 billion repurchasing 5 million shares, and it made no acquisitions after buying Payapps in fiscal 2025 [1]. At the current share price of $246.78, the stock trades well below the consensus target of $307.54 and a Buy rating, with a 52-week range of $215.01 to $329.09 [2][3].
market_position:
Autodesk's end market is global, and its growth is increasingly coming from outside the Americas. In fiscal 2026 the Americas delivered $3.18 billion of revenue, up 17%, which is 44% of the $7.21 billion total (calculated from the reported figures). EMEA delivered $2.79 billion (39%, up 21%) and APAC $1.23 billion (17%, up 11%, or 14% in constant currency) [1]. Foreign exchange was neutral to the 18% total growth, and international revenue stayed at 64% of the total in both fiscal 2026 and 2025 [1]. The filing flags weaker conditions in Brazil, India and China because of geopolitical conflict and trade wars, which limits how quickly APAC can grow [1].

Customer relationships are shifting from channel partners to Autodesk itself. Direct revenue rose 78% to $4.56 billion, or 63% of the total, while indirect revenue fell 26% to $2.65 billion [1]. TD Synnex dropped to 14% of revenue from 33%, and no other partner or direct customer reached 10% [1]. The 10-K names no blue-chip end customers beyond these channel partners, so the quality of the end-customer base cannot be verified from the filing. The direct model gives Autodesk more pricing control and customer data, but it also means Autodesk now carries the sales cost and commissions that partners previously absorbed [1].

Market share is not quantified in the 10-K, so position has to be read from scale and growth. Autodesk is a scaled incumbent leader in design and engineering software, with the largest revenue base in its peer set. Fiscal 2025 revenue of $6.13 billion compared with $1.50 billion at Bentley Systems, $2.74 billion at PTC and $1.32 billion at Procore [4]. Analysts expect FY2027 revenue of $8.37 billion, up 16.1%, with a consensus Buy rating and a $307.54 target price, both dated after the 10-K [3]. That path requires AECO and the direct channel to keep compounding, which is the main test for the coming year [1][3].
operating_results:
Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 18% to $7.21 billion, accelerating from 12% a year earlier, and subscription revenue supplied $1.03 billion of the $1.08 billion increase [1]. AECO led with 22% growth to $3.58 billion, while AutoCAD and AutoCAD LT grew 14%, Manufacturing 16% and Media and Entertainment 5% [1]. Gross margin held at 91.0%, but several costs grew faster than revenue. Marketing and sales rose 19% to $2.37 billion, mainly because Solution Provider commissions now sit in operating expense under the new transaction model, while R&D rose 11% to $1.64 billion and G&A rose 7% to $693 million [1]. Operating income rose 17% to $1.58 billion, so operating margin was flat at 22% [1]. Part of the reported growth is therefore presentation rather than volume, since incentives that used to reduce revenue now appear as expense [1].

Below the operating line, profit growth stalled. Restructuring charges rose to $216 million from $15 million, and tax expense climbed to $479 million from $272 million [1]. Net income rose only 1% to $1.12 billion, which is a 15.6% net margin on $7.21 billion of revenue (calculated), down from 18.1% a year earlier [1]. Diluted EPS rose 2% to $5.23, while non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 23% to $10.43, and non-GAAP operating margin widened to 38% from 36% [1]. The gap between GAAP and non-GAAP results is the key question for investors, because restructuring is expected to fall in fiscal 2027 and a GAAP margin gain would confirm the non-GAAP trend [1]. Geography was balanced: EMEA grew 21% to $2.79 billion, Americas 17% to $3.18 billion and APAC 11% to $1.23 billion, with foreign exchange neutral to growth [1].

Cash generation was the strongest part of the year. Operating cash flow rose to $2.45 billion from $1.61 billion, and free cash flow reached $2.38 billion [1][2]. Working capital absorbed $501 million, mainly from a $1.05 billion rise in prepaid and other assets [1]. The company repurchased 5 million shares for $1.40 billion and paid no dividend [1]. On consensus, analysts expect FY2027 revenue of $8.37 billion, up 16.1%, and normalized EPS of $12.80, figures dated after the 10-K [3]. Against peers, Autodesk's FY2025 revenue of $6.13 billion was the largest in its group, well ahead of Bentley, PTC and Procore [4].
risk_assessment:
The first risk is concentration. The AutoCAD and AutoCAD LT family made up 25% of fiscal 2026 revenue, down from 26%, and the filing notes that sales of these products have at times declined without a matching rise in collections or cloud revenue [1]. Distributor concentration has eased sharply, with TD Synnex falling to 14% of revenue from 33%, but the shift has moved sales cost and commissions onto Autodesk's own books [1]. The software industry faces low barriers to entry and AI that may change customer demand in unpredictable ways, so a franchise carrying a quarter of revenue is exposed to share loss [1].

The second risk is international exposure. About 64% of net revenue came from outside the United States in both years [1]. Trade policy has changed several times. The IEEPA-based tariffs were rescinded on February 24, 2026, but refunds remain uncertain, and a 10% temporary import surcharge under Section 122 applies from the same date to many of the same products [1]. Sanctions and export restrictions tied to Russia, China and the Middle East add further exposure, and the company says it does not fully hedge currency risk, with hedges running one to 18 months [1].

The third risk is execution during the transition. Billing timing has been distorted by the move to named-user plans and annual billing of multi-year contracts, and the filing expects this to continue into fiscal 2027 [1]. The January 2026 Plan is described as the final phase of the sales and marketing optimization program, but the filing warns that costs may exceed forecasts and savings may fall short [1]. Operating expenses are relatively fixed in the short term, so a revenue shortfall would hit profitability quickly [1]. Debt is manageable: $2.50 billion of principal matures between June 2027 and June 2035, and a $1.5 billion revolver is undrawn [1]. On the balance sheet, Yahoo Finance shows net debt of $137 million at fiscal year-end and net cash of $450 million at the latest quarter, with a current ratio of 0.9x [2]. The Altman Z-Score of 4.09 is in the safe zone, and the Beneish M-Score of -2.68 shows no statistical warning sign [2].

Governance is a watch item. The Audit Committee investigation into free cash flow and non-GAAP operating margin practices was closed by the SEC and the US Attorney's Office in August 2025, but shareholder litigation remains pending [1]. Because management guides investors on these metrics, any restatement would be material. Shares traded between $215 and $329 over the past 52 weeks, and the current price of $246.78 sits in the lower half of that range [2][3].
competitors_analysis:
Bentley Systems, PTC and Procore were chosen as peers on business model first. Bentley is named in the 10-K as a competitor and sells infrastructure engineering software, PTC sells subscription CAD and product lifecycle software, and Procore provides a cloud construction management platform that overlaps with Autodesk's construction cloud [1][4]. Size came second: Autodesk's FY2025 revenue of $6.13 billion was the largest in the group, against $1.50 billion at Bentley, $2.74 billion at PTC and $1.32 billion at Procore [4]. Trimble was closer in size (0.5x) but is less aligned with Autodesk's design-software model, so it ranked below these three.

Autodesk's gross margin of 90.6% in FY2025 was the highest of the group, while the other three sat in a 78% to 84% range [4]. Profitability is where it trails. Its EBITDA margin was 25.3% in FY2025, against 28.8% at Bentley and 41.3% at PTC, and Procore was close to break-even at 1.3% [4]. In FY2026 Autodesk's EBITDA margin improved to 27.6%, while PTC reached 54.9% on revenue that was flat at -0.2% [4]. Return on invested capital is the offsetting strength. Autodesk's ROIC of 22.4% in FY2025 was roughly double PTC's 15.9% and Bentley's 11.9%, and Procore remained negative at -5.5% [4]. Its FY2026 revenue growth of 17.5% also far exceeded PTC's [4].

On valuation, Autodesk's EV/EBITDA fell to 27.2 in FY2026 from 43.6 in FY2025, while PTC traded at 11.2 on EV/EBITDA, and Autodesk's EV/Sales of 7.5 compared with PTC's 6.2 [2][4]. The premium to PTC on sales is therefore smaller than the premium on EBITDA suggests. The premium is justified in part by ROIC and growth, but not by profitability, where PTC earns a far higher margin [4]. The resources do not explain the fall in the EV/EBITDA multiple, so it cannot be determined whether the lower multiple reflects share price weakness or higher EBITDA [2]. Autodesk would lose its quality premium if revenue growth fell back toward the 10% to 11% range of 2024 and 2025, or if ROIC dropped below 21.7%, its 2024 low [4].

investment_theses.thesis: AECO growth keeps total revenue growth above 15% in FY2027.
investment_theses.evidence: AECO rose 22% to $3.58 billion and subscription revenue supplied $1.03 billion of the $1.08 billion increase [1]. Consensus expects FY2027 growth of 16.1% [3].
investment_theses.signpost: Each FY2027 quarterly report shows total revenue growth of at least 15% and AECO growth of at least 18%.
investment_theses.invalidation: Total revenue growth falls below 12% for two consecutive quarters, or AECO growth falls below 15%.

investment_theses.thesis: GAAP operating margin rises above 22% in FY2027 as restructuring costs fall from $216 million.
investment_theses.evidence: Operating margin was flat at 22% in FY2026 while restructuring rose from $15 million to $216 million [1]. Non-GAAP operating margin widened to 38% from 36% [1].
investment_theses.signpost: The FY2027 annual report, due around March 2027, shows GAAP operating margin above 23% and restructuring below $100 million.
investment_theses.invalidation: Restructuring stays above $150 million in FY2027, or GAAP operating margin remains at or below 22%.

investment_theses.thesis: At the current price, the stock returns less than its cost of capital unless growth beats consensus.
investment_theses.evidence: The reverse DCF implies 11.3% annual revenue growth for ten years against a historical 12.9% three-year CAGR [2]. The consensus path yields a 9.5% IRR against an 11.1% WACC [3].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2027 consensus revenue holds at or above $8.37 billion through the next two quarterly updates, and FY2027 EPS estimates rise above $12.80.
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2027 consensus revenue is cut below $8.2 billion, which would make the growth path too weak to support the valuation.

investment_theses.thesis: Free cash flow stays above $2.0 billion in FY2027 even as billings move to annual installments.
investment_theses.evidence: Free cash flow reached $2.38 billion in FY2026 and operating cash flow $2.45 billion, although working capital absorbed $501 million [1]. Trailing free cash flow reached $2.80 billion at the latest quarter [2].
investment_theses.signpost: The FY2027 annual report, due around March 2027, shows free cash flow of at least $2.0 billion and deferred revenue growing at least as fast as revenue.
investment_theses.invalidation: Free cash flow falls below $2.0 billion, or buybacks are funded with new debt rather than operating cash flow.
